speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify your symptoms: do you experience specific eye movements like nystagmus, and have you noticed any tremors in your hands or speech difficulties? Additionally, have you had any recent falls or dizziness?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. Have you experienced any recent vision changes, specifically difficulty with eye movements like double vision, or any numbness/tingling in your limbs? Additionally, do you have a history of multiple sclerosis or other neurological conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a very important detail; natalizumab is known to carry a risk of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML). Given your history of Crohn's disease, MS, and this new gait ataxia, have you noticed any worsening of weakness in your arms or legs, or any changes in your vision like blind spots?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with and without contrast
REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide the latest MRI Brain images.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. Given the multifocal demyelinating lesions on MRI and your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab, this is a classic presentation of PML. We must immediately discontinue natalizumab and consider switching immunomodulatory therapies to halt disease progression. Do you have any current fevers or headaches?
